questions: Does either eyelid droop more as the day goes on?
Do you experience double vision that worsens with prolonged looking or reading?
Does your speech become slurred or nasal after speaking for several minutes?
Do you have difficulty swallowing, especially later in the day?
Do you have weakness in your neck, arms, or legs that worsens with activity and improves with rest?
Do you have frequent involuntary blinking or forceful closing of your eyes?
Do you have involuntary movements or spasms of your mouth, jaw, or tongue?
Do you have tremor in your hands when they are at rest?
Have you noticed stiffness or slowness of movement?
Have you had any recent facial weakness, numbness, or asymmetry?
Did the facial weakness begin suddenly, over a few minutes or hours?
Is the weakness mainly on one side of your face?
Is your forehead less wrinkled and your eyebrow weaker on the affected side?
Do you have weakness or numbness in an arm or leg on the same side?
Did the facial weakness follow an ear infection, ear pain, or a blistering rash near the ear?
Have you had difficulty closing the affected eye completely?
Has this facial asymmetry been present since childhood or for as long as you can remember?
Is the asymmetry most noticeable when you smile, speak, or show your teeth?
Is the weakness confined to the lower corner of your mouth, with normal movement of your forehead, eyelids, and cheeks?
Has the facial asymmetry been progressively worsening recently?
Have you ever had a stroke or other brain or nerve disorder?
Is the facial asymmetry more apparent at rest than when you voluntarily move your face?
Does one side of your face feel numb or have reduced sensation?
Have you noticed loss or alteration of taste on one side of your tongue?
Do you have hearing loss, ringing in the ear, or increased sensitivity to sounds on the affected side?
Can you tightly shut both eyes and puff out both cheeks equally?
Have you had recurrent episodes of facial weakness that later improve?
orders: Bedside cranial nerve VII examination, documenting forehead wrinkling, eyebrow elevation, forceful eye closure, nasolabial fold symmetry, smiling, showing the teeth, and cheek puffing.
Bedside ice-pack test applied to the more ptotic eyelid for 2 minutes, with pre- and post-test palpebral fissure measurement.
Serum acetylcholine-receptor (AChR) antibody panel, including binding, blocking, and modulating antibodies.
Repetitive nerve stimulation electrophysiology of the facial and proximal limb muscles.
served: lid position and measurement (MRD1 both sides)
